1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Dream Visions (1 Enoch 83-90) (c. 150 BC)

'I saw in a vision how the heaven collapsed and was borne off and fell to the earth' opens the first Dream Vision — Enoch's vision of the Flood as cosmic-symbolic event. The collapse of heaven (the firmament un-stoppered) and its fall onto earth pictures the de-creative reversal of the Genesis 1 separation. This visionary mode of recording the Flood prefigures the apocalyptic visionary mode of Daniel and Revelation: history is shown to the prophet in symbolic-cosmic dream form, not merely narrated. The Tewahedo Synaxarium's Noah liturgy on 10 Magabit explicitly includes Enochic dream-vision elements alongside the Genesis narrative.

1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Dream Visions (1 Enoch 83-90) (c. 150 BC)

'I lifted up my hands and prayed and besought and spake, and said: Destroy not the earth; for I have seen the affliction of the earth, and a great destruction. And my grandfather Mahalalel said to me: Wherefore criest thou so, my son?' — Mahalalel's question precedes his interpretation. Tewahedo catechetical tradition preserves the multi-generational form of prophetic transmission preserved here: prophecy is not a private possession but is interpreted across generations within the family-and-tradition that carries it.
